candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a patient with thymoma, hypogammaglobulinemia (decreased IgG, normal IgA/IgM), decreased B lymphocytes, and recurrent infections (respiratory, diarrhea), which are the defining features of Good syndrome. The oral erosions are a manifestation.

While the patient has oral erosions and a thymoma, which can be associated with paraneoplastic pemphigus, the immunofluorescence and antibody tests (ELISA, immunoblot) for pemphigus were negative. The primary immunodeficiency (hypogammaglobulinemia, B cell deficiency) points away from paraneoplastic pemphigus as the overarching diagnosis and towards Good syndrome.

Good syndrome is a specific type of thymoma-associated immunodeficiency characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia and B-cell lymphopenia. This candidate is a broader category that encompasses Good syndrome but lacks the specificity of the full reference diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Thymoma-associated Immunodeficiency as a component of Good syndrome
